rows.text: Doctor Octopus refills your hand to eight at the end of every turn. That single line changes what cards are good: emptying your hand stops being a cost. Lion's Eye Diamond, Null Brooch, Tolarian Winds and every "exile a blue card rather than pay" spell in the format become free, because the cards come straight back. The deck spends its whole hand every turn and is handed a new one.

rows.name: Doctor Octopus, Master Planner
rows.text: your maximum hand size is eight, and at the beginning of your end step you draw back up to eight. Other Villains get +2/+2 on top.

IMPORTANT: the refill has an intervening-if clause. If you have eight cards in hand at the beginning of your end step, the ability does not trigger AT ALL. Spend down to seven or fewer before you pass, every single turn.

rows.name: Stinging Study
rows.text: draws seven and loses seven with Doc Ock in the command zone or on the battlefield. It is a one-card refill that does not care whether he has been answered.

guide.title: Free spells, because the hand is free

rows.name: Force of Negation
rows.text: exile a blue card to counter their combo piece on their turn. The card you pitched is replaced at your end step.

rows.name: Misdirection
rows.text: the same cost, and it turns the removal spell aimed at Doc Ock back onto its caster.

rows.name: Commandeer
rows.text: seven mana or two blue cards. In this deck it costs nothing — steal their Rhystic Study, their wrath, or their tutor.

rows.name: March of Swirling Mist
rows.text: exile blue cards to slash the cost, then phase your board out of a wrath or phase their blockers out of the way.

rows.name: Pact of Negation
rows.text: free now, and the upkeep payment is easy in a deck with this much ritual mana.

rows.name: Fierce Guardianship
rows.text: free with your commander out.

rows.name: Deadly Rollick
rows.text: the same, pointed at a creature.

rows.name: Snuff Out
rows.text: four life instead of four mana.

rows.name: Lion's Eye Diamond
rows.text: three mana of any colour for a hand you are about to be given back. In most decks it is unplayable; here it is a Black Lotus with a delay.

rows.name: Skirge Familiar
rows.text: discard a card, add {B}. A full hand is eight black mana, and the hand comes back at end of turn. This is the deck's biggest mana engine.

rows.name: Bone Miser
rows.text: discard a land for {B}{B}, a spell for a card, a creature for a 2/2. Alongside Skirge Familiar each land discarded is a net profit.

rows.name: Dark Ritual
rows.text: the classic acceleration into a turn-three Doc Ock or an early Torment.

rows.name: Cabal Ritual
rows.text: with threshold on — and this deck fills its graveyard fast — it is five black mana for two.

rows.name: Basalt Monolith
rows.text: three mana that untaps for three, which is a mana sink with nothing else to do.

rows.name: Thran Dynamo
rows.text: three more, colourless, uncounterable.

rows.name: Cabal Coffers
rows.text: the payoff for a mostly-Swamp mana base.

rows.name: Dream Halls
rows.text: pay for spells by discarding a card of a shared colour. With a hand that refills to eight, this casts your whole hand for free every turn.

rows.name: Oskar, Rubbish Reclaimer
rows.text: every nonland card you discard may be cast straight out of the graveyard. Combined with Dream Halls, discarding to pay for one spell makes the discarded card castable too — the chain runs through your entire hand in a single turn.

rows.name: Containment Construct
rows.text: exiles each discarded card and lets you play it this turn.

rows.name: Moonstone, Harsh Mistress
rows.text: the same, with a window that lasts until the end of your next turn, on a Villain body Doc Ock pumps.

rows.name: Currency Converter
rows.text: banks the discards and turns them into Treasures and 2/2 Rogues later.

rows.name: Reanimate
rows.text: one mana for whatever fatty went to the yard.

rows.name: Animate Dead
rows.text: the second copy, and it can take a creature out of an opponent's graveyard.

rows.name: Living Death
rows.text: your graveyard is always the deepest at the table after a few refills. Everyone wipes and you rebuild.

rows.name: The Soul Stone
rows.text: once harnessed, a creature back from the graveyard every upkeep.

rows.name: Thought Gorger
rows.text: eats your hand for counters, then draws you a card for each one when it leaves — and Doc Ock has already replaced the hand you fed it.

rows.name: Psychic Corrosion
rows.text: two mill from each opponent for every card you draw. Doc Ock draws four or five a turn on his own, so this is roughly ten to fifteen mill per opponent per turn cycle. It is a genuine alternate win.

rows.name: Teferi's Ageless Insight
rows.text: doubles every draw after your first each turn, which doubles Psychic Corrosion and Sheoldred.

rows.name: Alhammarret's Archive
rows.text: the same doubling, plus double lifegain.

rows.name: Sheoldred, the Apocalypse
rows.text: two life per card you draw, two lost per card they draw. In a deck drawing this much it gains ten or more a turn.

rows.name: Ominous Seas
rows.text: a counter per draw. Eight counters is an 8/8 Kraken, and this deck gets there in two turns.

rows.name: Ledger Shredder
rows.text: connives on everyone's second spell, filtering for you and growing itself.

rows.name: Psychic Frog
rows.text: draws on connection and eats your excess cards for counters.

rows.name: Torment of Hailfire
rows.text: the finisher. With Skirge Familiar, the rituals and Cabal Coffers, X is routinely ten or more, and their answer is to lose everything.

rows.name: Grafted Skullcap
rows.text: an extra card every draw step, and it discards your hand at end step. Order it BEFORE Doc Ock's refill — but remember Doc Ock only triggers if you were already under eight cards.

rows.name: Tolarian Winds
rows.text: two mana, dump the hand, redraw it, and every discard payoff triggers.

rows.name: Zombie Infestation
rows.text: two cards for a 2/2, forever, at instant speed.

rows.name: Sickening Dreams
rows.text: discard X, deal X to every creature and every player. On a full hand it is a wrath and a burn spell at once.

rows.name: Null Brooch
rows.text: a hard counterspell that costs a hand you get back anyway.

rows.name: Archfiend of Ifnir
rows.text: every discard is a -1/-1 counter on each of their creatures. A full-hand dump is a one-sided board wipe.

rows.name: Windfall
rows.text: everyone dumps and redraws; you are the one with the payoffs.

rows.name: Dreamscape Artist
rows.text: turns spare lands and a discard into two basics, which feeds Cabal Coffers.

rows.name: Mana Drain
rows.text: counter, then spend the mana on Torment of Hailfire.

rows.name: Cyclonic Rift
rows.text: overloaded, it is the clear for a lethal attack or the answer to a locked board.

rows.name: Damnation
rows.text: an unconditional wrath in black.

rows.name: Toxic Deluge
rows.text: scales past indestructible and past any size.

rows.name: Withering Torment
rows.text: creature or enchantment at instant speed.

rows.name: Feed the Swarm
rows.text: the only clean enchantment answer in these colours, on a sorcery.

rows.name: Dauthi Voidwalker
rows.text: unblockable, exiles everything headed for their graveyards, and cashes in for a free cast of their best card.

rows.name: Beseech the Mirror
rows.text: bargain it and cast the tutored card for free. Usually Dream Halls, Skirge Familiar or Torment of Hailfire.

rows.name: Diabolic Intent
rows.text: a Zombie or Shapeshifter token becomes any card in the deck.

rows.name: Black Market Connections
rows.text: three effects a turn, and this deck can afford the life.

rows.name: Mystic Remora
rows.text: turns one through four, it draws more than anything else in the deck.

guide.title: What to keep in an opening hand

rows.text: Keep rituals and mana. Doc Ock costs seven, and the deck does very little until he lands — Dark Ritual, Sol Ring, Thran Dynamo and Cabal Coffers are what make him a turn-four play instead of a turn-seven one.
Count to seven before you pass the turn. Every turn. Casting one more spell, cycling something, or feeding Zombie Infestation is the difference between a full refill and no trigger at all.

rows.name: Skirge Familiar
rows.text: this is the card that converts the refill into a kill. With him out, a full hand is eight mana toward Torment of Hailfire, and you get the hand back before your next turn.

rows.name: Dream Halls
rows.text: it is symmetrical, so deploy it on a turn you can use it immediately. With Oskar out that is usually the turn you win.
